title: What’s the best way to read a book
paragraphs: Do you like to bury your head in a good book? Getting absorbed in a good story is a great way to relax. It improves your literacy, and, according to some experts, it’s good for your health as well. Studies show that it can increase our emotional intelligence as we understand a range of perspectives and motivations. But despite these benefits, does the way we consume a story make any difference?

For the purist, the only way to digest a good story is with a paperback or hardback book. Being in print, it’s possible to feel and even smell the book. And of course it’s very portable. But the traditional book has had a rival in recent years from e-books, which are read on e-readers or tablets. An ‘electronic’ book enables you to store hundreds of virtual books in one place and allows you to download books directly.

The e-book has become popular in schools, too, and according to one school in London, it’s encouraged more children to read. 11-year-old Summit told the BBC: “If you really want a book, you can just get it online. It’s so easy, and it’s made me read more. I probably read every day now.” For adults, e-books are certainly a lightweight way of accessing our favourite literature on the move.

The recent lockdowns due to the coronavirus pandemic have certainly given us all time to read more, and in the UK at least, sales of physical books have risen strongly. Last year, some 202 million paperbacks and hardbacks were sold, and the publishing industry hopes this trend will continue now that people have got into the habit of reading more.

But for those who can’t or don’t want to look at the text in a book, there are audiobooks to listen to. According to Clare Thorpe, writing for the BBC Culture website: “There are hugely ambitious productions using ensemble casts, specially created soundscapes and technological advances… some authors are even skipping print and writing exclusive audio content.” No matter what your reading preference, there’s no doubt we are spoilt for choice in how we access a good story.

vocabulary.example: The purist insists that classic novels should be read in their original language.
vocabulary.translation: 这位纯粹主义者坚持认为经典小说应该读原著。

vocabulary.example: I bought a cheap paperback version of the novel for the journey.
vocabulary.translation: 我买了一本便宜的平装版小说，以备旅途阅读。

vocabulary.example: The hardback of this book comes with a collector's edition box.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书的精装版配有收藏版礼盒。

vocabulary.entry: e-reader /ˈiː riːdə(r)/ n. 电子阅读器
vocabulary.example: An e-reader is designed to reduce eye strain during long reading sessions.
vocabulary.translation: 电子阅读器的设计初衷是减轻长时间阅读时的眼部疲劳。

vocabulary.example: The library has a large collection of virtual books available for download.
vocabulary.translation: 这家图书馆有大量可供下载的虚拟书籍。

vocabulary.example: The government launched a campaign to improve adult literacy in rural areas.
vocabulary.translation: 政府发起了一项提升农村地区成人读写能力的运动。

vocabulary.example: The novel offers a unique perspective on life in the 19th century.
vocabulary.translation: 这部小说以独特的视角展现了19世纪的生活风貌。

vocabulary.example: The teacher tried to understand the student's motivation for misbehaving.
vocabulary.translation: 老师试图弄清楚这个学生行为不当的动机。

vocabulary.example: She likes to consume poetry slowly before going to bed.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢睡前慢慢品读诗歌。

vocabulary.example: The new streaming service has become a strong rival to traditional TV networks.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新的流媒体服务已成为传统电视网的强劲竞争对手。

vocabulary.example: I often listen to an audiobook while commuting to work.
vocabulary.translation: 我经常在通勤上班的路上听有声书。

vocabulary.entry: ensemble cast /ɒnˈsɒmbl kɑːst/ n. 全体配音阵容
vocabulary.example: The audiobook features an ensemble cast of famous voice actors.
vocabulary.translation: 这本有声书由一众著名配音演员组成的全体阵容演绎。

vocabulary.example: The soundscape of the audiobook makes listeners feel like they are in a forest.
vocabulary.translation: 这本有声书的音效场景让听众仿佛置身于森林之中。

vocabulary.example: The author wrote an exclusive story for the magazine's special edition.
vocabulary.translation: 这位作家为该杂志的特刊撰写了一篇独家报道。

vocabulary.entry: publishing industry /ˈpʌblɪʃɪŋ ˈɪndəstri/ n. 出版业
vocabulary.example: The publishing industry has adapted to the rise of digital reading.
vocabulary.translation: 出版业已适应了数字阅读的兴起。

vocabulary.example: There is a growing trend of people choosing to read physical books again.
vocabulary.translation: 人们重新选择阅读纸质书的趋势日益明显。

vocabulary.example: This lightweight laptop is perfect for people who travel a lot.
vocabulary.translation: 这款轻便的笔记本电脑非常适合经常出差的人。

vocabulary.example: The course covers classic and modern literature from around the world.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程涵盖了世界各地的经典与现代文学作品。

vocabulary.entry: on the move /ɒn ðə muːv/ 在行进中；在移动中
vocabulary.example: The app allows you to access your files easily when you're on the move.
vocabulary.translation: 这款应用能让你在出行途中轻松调取自己的文件。

vocabulary.example: The city imposed a lockdown to control the spread of the virus.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市实施了封锁，以控制病毒的传播。

vocabulary.entry: pandemic /pænˈdemɪk/ n. （全国或全球性）流行病
vocabulary.example: The pandemic has changed people's habits of work and life.
vocabulary.translation: 这场流行病改变了人们的工作和生活习惯。

vocabulary.example: Students can access the online library resources 24 hours a day.
vocabulary.translation: 学生们可以全天候获取线上图书馆的资源。

vocabulary.example: My personal preference is for books with simple but elegant covers.
vocabulary.translation: 我个人偏爱封面简约雅致的书籍。

vocabulary.entry: be spoilt for choice /biː spɔɪlt fɔː tʃɔɪs/ 选择太多而难以抉择
vocabulary.example: In this supermarket, you're spoilt for choice when it comes to fresh fruit.
vocabulary.translation: 这家超市的新鲜水果种类繁多，让人挑花了眼。

vocabulary.example: You can download the book to your device and read it offline.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以把这本书下载到设备上，离线阅读。

sentences.chinese: 你喜欢沉浸在一本好书里吗？

sentences.english: Getting absorbed in a good story is a great way to relax.
sentences.chinese: 全身心投入一个精彩的故事，是一种绝佳的放松方式。

sentences.english: It improves your literacy, and, according to some experts, it’s good for your health as well.
sentences.chinese: 阅读能提升你的读写能力，而且据一些专家称，它对健康也大有裨益。

sentences.english: Studies show that it can increase our emotional intelligence as we understand a range of perspectives and motivations.
sentences.chinese: 研究表明，在阅读过程中，我们会了解到许多观点与动机，这有助于提高情商。

sentences.english: But despite these benefits, does the way we consume a story make any difference?
sentences.chinese: 但抛开这些益处不谈，我们阅读故事的方式，是否会带来不一样的体验呢？

sentences.english: For the purist, the only way to digest a good story is with a paperback or hardback book.
sentences.chinese: 对于纯粹主义者而言，品读一本好书的唯一方式，就是阅读平装书或精装书。

sentences.english: Being in print, it’s possible to feel and even smell the book. And of course it’s very portable.
sentences.chinese: 纸质书可以触摸，甚至还能闻到纸张的气息，而且它的便携性也毋庸置疑。

sentences.english: But the traditional book has had a rival in recent years from e-books, which are read on e-readers or tablets.
sentences.chinese: 但近年来，传统书籍遇到了一个竞争对手——电子书，这类书籍需要借助电子阅读器或平板电脑来阅读。

sentences.english: An ‘electronic’ book enables you to store hundreds of virtual books in one place and allows you to download books directly.
sentences.chinese: 一本“电子”书能让你在同一个设备里储存数百本虚拟书籍，还支持直接下载。

sentences.english: The e-book has become popular in schools, too, and according to one school in London, it’s encouraged more children to read.
sentences.chinese: 电子书在学校里也十分受欢迎，伦敦的一所学校表示，电子书激发了更多孩子去阅读。

sentences.english: 11-year-old Summit told the BBC: “If you really want a book, you can just get it online.
sentences.chinese: 11岁的萨米特在接受BBC采访时说：“如果你特别想看一本书，直接上网就能找到。

sentences.english: It’s so easy, and it’s made me read more.
sentences.chinese: 这太方便了，也让我读了更多书。

sentences.english: I probably read every day now.”
sentences.chinese: 我现在几乎每天都会阅读。”

sentences.english: For adults, e-books are certainly a lightweight way of accessing our favourite literature on the move.
sentences.chinese: 对成年人来说，电子书无疑是一种轻便的方式，能让他们在出行途中随时阅读喜爱的文学作品。

sentences.english: The recent lockdowns due to the coronavirus pandemic have certainly given us all time to read more, and in the UK at least, sales of physical books have risen strongly.
sentences.chinese: 近年来，新冠疫情引发的封锁让人们有了更多时间阅读，至少在英国，纸质书的销量大幅上涨。

sentences.english: Last year, some 202 million paperbacks and hardbacks were sold, and the publishing industry hopes this trend will continue now that people have got into the habit of reading more.
sentences.chinese: 去年，平装书和精装书的销量约达2.02亿本，出版业希望，在人们养成了更频繁的阅读习惯后，这一趋势能够持续下去。

sentences.english: But for those who can’t or don’t want to look at the text in a book, there are audiobooks to listen to.
sentences.chinese: 而对于那些无法或不愿阅读纸质文字的人来说，有声书是不错的选择。

sentences.english: According to Clare Thorpe, writing for the BBC Culture website: “There are hugely ambitious productions using ensemble casts, specially created soundscapes and technological advances… some authors are even skipping print and writing exclusive audio content.”
sentences.chinese: 克莱尔·索普在为BBC文化频道撰稿时表示：“如今的有声书制作规模宏大，会启用全体配音阵容，搭配专门制作的音效场景，还融入了先进技术……有些作家甚至跳过纸质出版环节，直接创作独家有声内容。”

sentences.english: No matter what your reading preference, there’s no doubt we are spoilt for choice in how we access a good story.
sentences.chinese: 无论你偏爱哪种阅读方式，毫无疑问，我们如今在接触精彩故事的途径上，已经有了太多选择。
